newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA PRIVATISATION INFLOWS NOT TO HIT INFLATION.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA PRIVATISATION INFLOWS NOT TO HIT INFLATION.

text.p: Recent foreign exchange inflows from the privatisation of Sri Lanka's state-owned companies will not fuel inflation in the country, Central Bank governor Amarananda Jayawardena told Reuters on Thursday.

The government said on Tuesday it was using part of the $225 million raised from the sale of a 35 percent stake in Sri Lanka Telecom to Japan's Nippon Telephone and Telegraphic Corp (NTT) to retire 10 billion rupees worth of treasury bills.
"We are retiring 10 billion rupees worth of Treasury Bills from the Central Bank's portfolio, to make sure that it does not fuel inflation," Jayawardena said.
The remainder of the proceeds will be held by the Treasury as a deposit in the Central Bank, he said.
"The purpose is to sterilise the impact of this large inflow from having an impact on the domestic market," Jayawardena said.
Sri Lanka's average annual inflation fell to 13.9 percent in July from 14.7 in June.
Jayawardena said the yearly average should ease to single digit by the end of 1997, compared to 15.9 in 1996.
